g6-2023-003.stem: A bakery owner bakes 450 cookies each day. Which equation can be used to determine the number of cookies, c, the owner bakes for any number of days, d ?

existingEvidence.quote: Select all equations that can represent the relationship between b , cups of

g6-2023-003.why: The item asks which equation relates cookies c to days d at 450 per day. The Cool-down gives a constant-ratio table and asks which equations can represent the relationship between the two variables, with the reversed-variable distractors the item also uses.

g6-2023-012.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 14 less than the product of 8 and y ?

existingEvidence.quote: Circle the expression that represents the number of inches the plant grew

g6-2023-012.why: The item asks which expression is "14 less than the product of 8 and y," where the trap is writing 14 − 8y. The Cool-down makes students choose between x − 8 and 8 − x for a "grew by" comparison — the same order-of-subtraction decision.

g6-2023-014.stem: What is the value of the expression 3(7−2)+532 ?

existingEvidence.quote: students use the order of operations to find the value of expressions

g6-2023-014.why: The item evaluates (3(7−2)+5^3)/2, which needs the parentheses, then the exponent, then the division. The Row Game is a column of numeric expressions with exponents that students evaluate by the order of operations, which is exactly the demand.

g6-2023-022.stem: What is the value of the expression 5b + c3 when b = 7 and c = 4 ?

existingEvidence.quote: They evaluate expressions when given a value for the variable.

g6-2023-022.why: The item evaluates 5b + c^3 at b = 7, c = 4. The activity is a list of expressions with exponents and coefficients to evaluate at a given value of the variable.

g6-2023-024.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 8 (2a + 3b) − 2b ?

existingEvidence.activity: Writing Equivalent Expressions Using the Distributive Property
existingEvidence.quote: students generate equivalent algebraic expressions using the distributive property

g6-2023-024.why: The item needs 8(2a + 3b) − 2b = 16a + 22b: distribute over two unlike terms, then collect the b terms. The distributing half is this activity (y(3x + 4z) is a row); the collecting half is not asked anywhere in grade 6. Optional lesson; non-optional runner-up is Lesson 10, "Areas of Partitioned Rectangles."

g6-2023-040.stem: Lee makes a rectangular-shaped tile pattern by placing three tiles side by side, with no space between the tiles. The list below describes the shape of each tile and the order in which they are placed. • The first tile is in the shape of a square with side lengths of x inches. • The middle tile is shaped like a rectangle with a width of x inches and a length of 3x inches. • The third tile is shaped like a square with side lengths of x inches. The perimeter of the tile pattern is 60 inches. What is the value of x in the tile pattern?

existingEvidence.activity: Partitioned Rectangles When Lengths Are Unknown
existingEvidence.quote: students use expressions with variables to represent lengths of sides and areas

g6-2023-040.why: The item composes a square, a 3x-by-x rectangle and a square into one rectangle and solves 12x = 60 from its perimeter. Composing rectangles with an unknown side and writing expressions for the composite is this activity; writing a perimeter expression and solving back for the unknown is not asked anywhere in grade 6, which fits the item’s p-value of 0.13.

g6-2023-043.stem: What is the value of the expression 7 × (5 − 3)3 − 20 ÷ 4 ?

existingEvidence.quote: use the order of operations to find the value of expressions with exponents

g6-2023-043.why: The item evaluates 7 × (5−3)^3 − 20 ÷ 4. The Row Game rows have the same shape — a product with an exponent plus or minus a second term — and are worked by the order of operations.

g6-2023-046.stem: Logan earns money for completing chores. The graph shown below represents the relationship between the number of chores, x, he completes, and the amount o f money, y, he earns. Based on the graph, explain the relationship between the number of chores Logan completes and the amount of money he earns. Be sure to identify the dependent and the independent variables in your answer. Determine the total amount of money Logan will earn after completing 9 chores.
figures: Three points rise steadily: 1 chore at 4.50 dollars, 2 at 9, and 3 at 13.50.

existingEvidence.quote: What point on the graph would represent the time it takes the robot

g6-2023-046.why: The item reads a graph of chores against money, asks for the relationship and the dependent and independent variables, then for the earnings at 9 chores. The Cool-down asks which variable is independent, what a plotted point means, and what point would represent a value off the plotted range.

g6-2024-002.stem: Which expression represents 5 more than the product of 2 and y ?

existingEvidence.quote: Write expressions to show Clare’s age when her cousin is at different ages.

g6-2024-002.why: The item asks for "5 more than the product of 2 and y" (2y + 5). This activity builds exactly those two pieces: x + 5 for "5 years older" and 3n for "3 times as many."

g6-2024-003.stem: Which value of b makes the inequality 3b > 12 true?

existingEvidence.quote: a number that can be used in place of the variable to make

g6-2024-003.why: The item asks which value of b makes 3b > 12 true. This is the activity that defines a solution to an inequality as a value that makes it true and has students decide whether given heights qualify.

g6-2024-014.stem: What is the value of the expression 82 ÷ 4 × 23 ?

existingEvidence.quote: students extend their understanding of the order of operations to include expressions with

g6-2024-014.why: The item is 8^2 ÷ 4 × 2^3: the powers must be found before the multiplication and division. Jada and Noah argue over exactly that in 6 · 10^2, one squaring first and one multiplying first.

g6-2024-022.stem: Tammy and Jacob collect stamps. Tammy has s stamps. Jacob has 4 fewer than 3 times the number of stamps Tammy has. Which expression can be used to represent the number of stamps Jacob has?

existingEvidence.quote: Write expressions that can show how many comic books Diego has for different

g6-2024-022.why: The item wants 3s − 4 for "4 fewer than 3 times the number of stamps Tammy has." This activity writes 3n for "3 times as many comic books" and x + 5 for an age comparison; the item combines the two steps.

g6-2024-038.stem: What value of n makes the equation n8 = 17 true?

existingEvidence.quote: Solve each equation. Explain or show your reasoning.

g6-2024-038.why: The item asks for the value of n making n/8 = 17 true. The Cool-down is three equations of the forms x + p = q and px = q to be solved, including a fractional-coefficient one.

g6-2024-041.stem: A student claims that the expression 6 + 8x is equivalent to the expression 3 (3 + 5x). What is incorrect about the student’s claim? Be sure to include an equivalent expression to 3 (3 + 5x) in your response.

existingEvidence.quote: Select all the expressions that represent the large rectangle’s total area.

g6-2024-041.why: The item asks why 6 + 8x is not equivalent to 3(3 + 5x) and wants a correct equivalent. This Cool-down asks students to separate correct distributions (5(b + 3), 5b + 15) from a plausible wrong one (3(5 + b)) for the same rectangle.

g6-2025-005.stem: What is the value of the expression shown below when c = 2 and h = 3 ?

existingEvidence.quote: Find the value of each expression for the given value of x

g6-2025-005.why: The item evaluates c^3 + 4h − 7 at c = 2, h = 3. The Cool-down is the same task — 4 + x^2, 4^x, 4x at a given value — and is where the curriculum tests it.

g6-2025-019.stem: What is the value of the expression shown below?

existingEvidence.quote: Find the value of the expressions in one of the columns.

g6-2025-019.why: The item evaluates (3^2 + 5·3)/2^3, with exponents in both numerator and denominator. The Row Game asks for the value of exactly this kind of multi-operation expression with exponents.

g6-2025-023.stem: What is the coefficient in the expression 2x3?

existingEvidence.quote: when considering the difference between expressions like 3 x and 3x

g6-2025-023.why: The item asks for the coefficient in 2x^3, where the distractor is the exponent 3. The activity is built on telling 3^x from 3x and uses "coefficient" and "exponent" as the words for that difference.

g6-2025-027.stem: Which number is not a solution to the inequality shown below?

existingEvidence.quote: Select all numbers that are solutions to the inequality w < 1 .

g6-2025-027.why: The item asks which number is NOT a solution to 3w ≥ 12. The Cool-down is the same sorting of candidate values into solutions and non-solutions of a given inequality.

g6-2025-030.stem: Which expression represents the phrase “the sum of fifteen and five less than twice a number, n ” ?

existingEvidence.quote: Another esport player scored p fewer points than Priya. Write an expression

g6-2025-030.why: The item wants "the sum of fifteen and five less than twice a number n" — 15 + (2n − 5). This activity writes a comparison expression with a variable (473 − p), but nothing in grade 6 nests two operations inside one phrase, which is why confidence is low and the item’s p-value is 0.26.

g6-2025-040.stem: What is the value of the expression 4 (3 + 52) − 6 ?

existingEvidence.quote: Jada says the total volume is 27,000 cubic inches. Noah says it is

g6-2025-040.why: The item is 4(3 + 5^2) − 6, whose trap is adding 3 + 5 before squaring. The Cool-down is that error exactly: Jada computes (20 + 10)^3 while Noah computes 20 + 10^3.

g6-2025-046.stem: The figure below shows the dimensions of a rug shaped like a rectangle. The area of the rug is 54 square feet. Write and solve an equation to determine the value of x. Be sure to use the unknown, x, in your equation. Answerx = A company buys 7 of these rugs for $784. Write and solve an equation to determine the price, p, of each rug. Be sure to use the unknown, p, in your equation.
figures: The rectangle is 9 feet wide and 2x feet tall.

existingEvidence.quote: practice matching equations to situations and then solving those equations using their choice

g6-2025-046.why: The item asks students to write and solve an equation twice — 9 · 2x = 54 for the rug and 7p = 784 for the price. This activity is write-or-choose-then-solve for situations of exactly the px = q shape (the solar-panel question is 1.5p = 100).

g6-2026-004.stem: An expression is shown below. What is the value of the expression when x = 7 and y = 3 ?

existingEvidence.quote: they also deepen their understanding of the order of operations

g6-2026-004.why: The item evaluates 2(12 − x) + y^2 at x = 7, y = 3, so a substitution has to be followed through parentheses and a power. This activity is where substitution and the order of operations are worked together.

g6-2026-019.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 5 (6m + 3) + 4m ?

existingEvidence.activity: Writing Equivalent Expressions Using the Distributive Property
existingEvidence.quote: They practice writing a sum or difference when given a product

g6-2026-019.why: The item needs 5(6m + 3) + 4m = 34m + 15, again distribute-then-collect. Only the distributing step is practised here, and in an optional lesson; non-optional runner-up is Lesson 10, "Areas of Partitioned Rectangles."

g6-2026-023.stem: At an amusement park, a rider must be at least 48 inches tall to ride a roller coaster. Which number line represents how tall, in inches, a rider must be to ride the roller coaster?
figures: Each runs from 45 to 55. They differ in whether the circle at 48 is filled or open and in whether the ray shaded runs to the left or to the right.

existingEvidence.quote: represent each height requirement on a number line

g6-2026-023.why: The item asks which number line shows "a rider must be at least 48 inches tall." The activity is amusement-park height requirements, including a "58 inches minimum," written as inequalities and graphed on number lines.

g6-2026-026.stem: An inequality is shown below. Which value of k makes the inequality true?

existingEvidence.quote: determining whether a value is a solution to one or more of the

g6-2026-026.why: The item asks which value of k makes k − 16 > 29 true. Deciding whether a particular number satisfies a stated inequality is precisely the reasoning in the ride-height questions.

g6-2026-027.stem: A bakery sells boxes of cookies. The list below shows information for one month of sales. • The bakery sold a total of 324 boxes of cookies. • Of the boxes sold, 250 of the boxes contained just chocolate chip cookies. • The rest of the boxes sold contained just sugar cookies. Which equation can be used to determine the total number of boxes, x, of sugar cookies sold by the bakery that month?

existingEvidence.quote: students select an equation with a variable that can represent a situation with

g6-2026-027.why: The item asks which equation determines the number of sugar-cookie boxes, x + 250 = 324. Storytime is three situations against six candidate equations, including the x + 5 = 20 versus x + 20 = 5 confusion the distractors exploit.

g6-2026-030.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 55 less than the sum of 4 and twice a number, c ?

existingEvidence.quote: students relate quantities in situations to numerical and variable expressions

g6-2026-030.why: The item wants "55 less than the sum of 4 and twice a number c" — (4 + 2c) − 55. The activity practises the "fewer than" ordering with a variable, but again only one operation at a time.

g6-2026-032.stem: An expression is shown below. Which expression is equivalent to the expression shown?

existingEvidence.activity: Writing Equivalent Expressions Using the Distributive Property
existingEvidence.quote: a product when given a sum or difference

g6-2026-032.why: The item factors 24x + 18y into 6(4x + 3y). This activity’s table runs in that direction too (4x − 20, 10x − 5 must be written as products). Optional lesson; the non-optional runner-up is Lesson 10, Activity "Partitioned Rectangles When Lengths Are Unknown," where 8 · 5 + 5x is rewritten as the product 5(8 + x).

g6-2026-038.stem: What is the coefficient in the expression 6n5?

existingEvidence.quote: practice using mathematical vocabulary related to expressions, such as “coefficient,”

g6-2026-038.why: The item asks for the coefficient in 6n^5. Same activity, same discrimination between the number in front and the number above; the vocabulary is named in the Activity Synthesis rather than practised in a task.

g6-2026-041.stem: Bella has a collection of 150 baseball cards. Dan has 43 fewer baseball cards in his collection than Bella has. Write and solve an equation to determine how many baseball cards, c, Dan has.

existingEvidence.quote: Kiran scores 223 fewer points in a computer game than Mai.

g6-2026-041.why: The item asks students to write and solve an equation for "Dan has 43 fewer cards than Bella’s 150." The activity’s first question is the same sentence with different numbers, with the same competing equations to sort out.

existingEvidence.quote: Find the value of the expressions in one of the columns.

g6-2026-045.why: The item evaluates 3(4^3 − 6^2) + 7(2 + 1)^3 — two groupings, three powers. The Row Game is the only place students are asked to find the values of expressions with exponents at this level of nesting.
